situation.problem_text:
Topic: Exploring the 2-adic Metric: Where Infinite Sums Behave Differently

Target audience: Undergraduate mathematics students

Section: section_1 — The Familiar World: Euclidean Distance

Lecture lines:
Standard distance is the real line.
We measure distance by |x minus y|.
Series converge as points get closer.

Planned animations:
Draw Euclidean distance between two points (x1, y1) and (x2, y2) in #FFFFFF.
Highlight the squared differences: (x2-x1)^2 and (y2-y1)^2 in #FFD700.
Combine these into the distance formula: sqrt((x2-x1)^2 + (y2-y1)^2) in #00FFFF.
Animate point movement to show standard continuous distance change.
Label 'Euclidean Metric' clearly in #FFFFFF below the formula.

Section: section_2 — The 2-adic Perspective: Defining the Valuation

Lecture lines:
The 2-adic valuation counts powers of 2.
We define 2-adic absolute value as 2 power -v2(x).
In this world, powers of 2 are tiny.

Planned animations:
Display the integer n = 2^k * m in #FFFFFF.
Isolate the power k as the 2-adic valuation v2(n).
Animate k increasing as n becomes more divisible by 2.

Section: section_3 — The Non-Archimedean Mystery

Lecture lines:
The ultrametric inequality defines 2-adic space.
It forces a no-carry logic.
Balls either do not intersect or nest.

Planned animations:
Show the ultrametric inequality: d(x, z) <= max(d(x, y), d(y, z)) in #FFFFFF.
Visualize three points x, y, z forming an isosceles triangle.
Highlight that the longest side length is at most equal to the others in #FF4500.

Section: section_4 — Infinite Sums: Convergence Reversal

Lecture lines:
Infinite sums behave differently here.
The series 1+2+4+8 converges to -1.
Terms must approach zero in the 2-adic sense.

Planned animations:
Show the sequence of partial sums of 1 + 2 + 4 +... in #FFFFFF.
Show the 2-adic partial sums approaching -1 in #FFD700.
Transition from divergent in R to convergent in Q2 in #00FFFF.

Section: section_5 — Conclusion: A New Mathematical Reality

Lecture lines:
Changing distance metrics shifts convergence.
2-adic analysis reveals deep hidden structure.
This is vital for modern number theory.

Planned animations:
Summarize R (Euclidean) vs Q2 (2-adic) side-by-side in #FFFFFF.
Animate zooming out to show two distinct number lines.
Show Q2 as a fragmented structure using a fractal-like visual.

Apply a scale_factor between 0.7 and 0.8 to text labels within the animation grid to ensure they remain visually subordinate to primary mobjects and prevent horizontal crowding.
When displaying multiple distinct primary components in a two-column layout, vertically divide the 6x6 grid into segments (e.g., Rows A-C and Rows D-F) and assign each component to its own segment.

import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]

        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)

                y = 2.2 - i * 1

        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]

        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2

        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
